description: A broad extraction of an iOS full file-system acquisition (a tar, plain or compressed, or a zip): iLEAPP's artefact modules run over the whole of it and write a TSV report per artefact that has records, a timeline database and an HTML report, the searchable form of what the phone holds. The run reads iLEAPP's own log for one outcome per module (modules.tsv: completed, no_record, unsupported, errored, errors_logged or unknown) and says complete only when iLEAPP exited 0, wrote a TSV report, the log was recognised, says how many modules it parses and that many started, ends with its processing-completed line, no module errored, logged an error or is unknown, no line outside a module speaks of an error and stderr holds nothing the log shape does not explain.
exclusions: artefacts no module of the pinned iLEAPP release parses: their files stay in the source, unread by this extraction
deleted records beyond what a module reads itself (SQLite free pages, WAL): nothing is carved
protected data that needs a key it does not have (keychain secrets, data protection classes locked in the acquisition)
a module the log does not account for as completed (errored, or started and not finished): see modules.tsv
covers: What iLEAPP's modules parse from the whole acquisition: one TSV per artefact that has records, its timeline and every file it wrote, kept under ileapp/, and modules.tsv with the outcome of each module its log names. A module that finds nothing writes no report (no_record), which does not show the artefact never existed, and a module whose own gate does not take the operating-system version (unsupported) read nothing of that artefact; files no module targets are not read; a module that errored or whose end the log does not show is not covered, however many reports the others wrote. The report contains the phone's own content and is a sensitive output.
